Re-operation is a procedural event recognized as a severe and difficult disease complication following primary surgical interventions in patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) [^src1]. Because it places a substantial burden on both the patient and the hospital system, it is closely tracked as a critical measure of surgical quality [^src1].

In the context of the 2024 DANIBD report, re-operations occurring within 30 days of the initial surgery are monitored specifically by [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] [^src1]. The 2024 data revealed that this complication occurred in 13% of all surgical interventions nationwide [^src1]. The report underscores that the national targets for this indicator were not met, highlighting significant regional variation and ongoing challenges in optimizing surgical outcomes and minimizing post-operative complications for IBD patients [^src1].
